Soccer",{"abbrev":297,"shortDisplay":297,"shortName":299,"globalSportId":242,"globalSportNameSlug":300,"globalSportGender":250,"id":301,"title":115},"2025-11-17T11:51:56.763","/sports/womens-soccer/roster/christine-erdman/19872",[4241,4271,4298],{"bio":4242,"twitter":21,"image":4243,"images":15,"displayFields":4247,"sport":4251,"latestCoachBioId":4252,"latestSupportBioId":15,"latestBioId":4252,"id":4253,"title":4254,"firstName":4255,"lastName":4256,"email":4257,"phone":21,"url":15,"staffId":4258,"socialMediaR":4259,"custom1":21,"custom2":21,"custom3":21,"custom4":21},"Chris Fox begins his second season as head coach of the Bowling Green State University women's soccer program in the fall of 2025. Fox, the architect of an impressive turnaround at Morehead State, came to BGSU after two years with the Eagles..\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Ca href=\"/galleries//122123-chris-fox-press-conference-wsoc/2409\">\u003Cstrong>PHOTO GALLERY: Chris Fox Press Conference (Dec. 21, 2023)\u003C/strong>\u003C/a>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"The BGSU family is excited to welcome Coach Chris Fox, his wife Emily, and their family to our Bowling Green community,\" said BGSU Director of Athletics Derek van der Merwe at the time of Fox's hiring in December of 2023. \"Coach Fox is an experienced leader who knows how to build successful organizations and programs. He is passionate about details, values, discipline, and the holistic development of student-athletes.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"He is committed to the student-athlete experience, placing genuine value on the educational process. His dedication and philosophy make him the ideal choice for BGSU.\"He has contributed to multiple conference championships and NCAA Tournament appearances at various stops in his career, and we are honored to have him join our team and our quest for excellence.\"\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn his first season at the helm, Fox and the Falcons went 7-7-4 overall and 4-4-3 in Mid-American Conference play. BGSU finished with a 4-1-3 record at Cochrane Stadium in 2024, and advanced to the MAC Tournament for the eighth consecutive season, the longest current streak in the conference.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nFour Falcons earned all-league honors, as Lexi Czerwien was named to the All-MAC First Team while Emme Butera garnered All-MAC Second-Team honors. First-year Falcons Payton O'Malley and Haley Wolf were named to the MAC's All-Freshman Team.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn the classroom, six Falcons were named to the Academic All-District Team, selected by College Sports Communicators, while a total of 13 Falcons were named to the Academic All-MAC Team.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nFox assumed the helm of the Morehead State program in 2022, taking over a program that had won a total of 18 games in the previous five seasons, and proceeded to lead the Eagles to a 7-7-4 record in that '22 campaign, followed by a 9-6-5 mark in 2023.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThe Eagles, who went 6-18-4 in Ohio Valley Conference play in the three seasons from 2019-21, posted a 4-2-2 league mark in the 2022 campaign.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThen, in 2023, MSU went 6-1-2 in OVC regular-season play to finish second in the conference, then won the league tournament to advance to the NCAA Championships. Fox was named a 2023 OVC co-Coach of the Year.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThe team's overall record of 9-6-5 in the fall of 2023 was the team's best mark since 2015.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\n\"I am excited and honored to be named the next women's soccer head coach at Bowling Green State University,\" said Fox at the time of his hiring at BGSU. \"I would like to thank Athletic Director Derek van der Merwe, President Rogers and the rest of the athletic administration for placing their trust in me to lead the program.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"I want to thank Morehead State University for giving me the opportunity to become a head coach and for all of their support during my time there. A special thank you to all of the players for their unwavering commitment, hard work and passion in reshaping Morehead State soccer. It was an honor to work with you all and I will forever cherish those relationships.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"I believe that BG Soccer will continue to be a force in the MAC. My family and I are looking forward to immersing ourselves in the Bowling Green community and I cannot wait to get started.\"\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nFox's guidance led to immense success in 2022 as the Eagles finished with seven wins and four OVC wins. The program achieved a plethora of accolades and accomplishments including the highest OVC finish since 2013 (third), the most wins since 2015 (7), the third-longest unbeaten streak (6) in program history, the fewest losses since 2014, and the fewest goals allowed in program history (21).\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn addition, Fox's style of play led to ample opportunities for student-athletes to achieve a high number of individual honors, including the program's first clean sweep of all three OVC weekly awards (Offensive Player, Defensive Player and Goalkeeper of the Week) since 2007, and the program's first All-OVC First-Team honoree since 2018.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThen, in 2023, Fox and the Eagles enjoyed many more accolades, including the program's most all-conference selections (five) since 1999 and the OVC Tournament MVP (Kate Larbes).\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nAfter a 1-4-3 start to the season, the Eagles then went 8-1-2 over the next 11 contests, all against OVC foes. That 11-game run ended with a six-match winning streak that spanned the end of the regular season and the conference tournament.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThe Eagles allowed just four goals in those 11 matches, with eight shutouts during that time. In all, MSU posted nine shutouts on the season, the second-highest total in program history.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nFox joined the Eagles after spending four highly-successful seasons with High Point University, starting as an assistant coach and recruiting coordinator before being promoted to associate head coach in 2020.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nDuring his four seasons at HPU, the team enjoyed the most successful period in program history, which culminated in a Big South Conference title and NCAA Tournament berth in the fall of 2021.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nStarting with nearly a complete rebuild in 2018 due to extensive graduation losses from the year before, it only took Fox and the staff one year to ascend to the top. In 2019, High Point set Big South records by going undefeated and winning the regular season title.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn the spring of 2021 (fall season moved due to COVID), the program bettered that record by winning the regular-season title with a perfect 8-0 mark, while only conceding three goals. Fox's expertise helped head coach Brandi Fontaine win Big South Coach of the Year in back-to-back seasons. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nWith Fox on staff, HPU rose as high as No. 6 in the RPI and No. 8 in the United Soccer Coaches Southeast Region, and the program received top-25 votes from United Soccer Coaches, Top Drawer Soccer and College Soccer News across multiple weeks in the spring 2021 season. All of these rankings were program bests. High Point also ranked top-10 in the nation in several stat categories: scoring offense, goals against average, save percentage, winning pct. and points per game.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nFox was directly responsible for the recruitment and development of four High Point United Soccer Coaches All-Southeast Region Players, one Big South Attacking Player of the Year, two Big South Freshmen of the Year, seven First-Team all-conference players and five Second-Team all-conference players. Two of these players have since signed professional contracts with S.S. Lazio and AS St-Étienne in Italy and France, respectively, another program first.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nBefore joining the staff at High Point, Fox spent 10 years in Pennsylvania working on the club circuit for HMMS Eagle FC. Fox guided a number of teams to great success, including his 1999 girls' team, which featured more than 20 future collegiate players, wins in the Region 1 Premier League, Jefferson Cup and Disney Showcase, as well as a No. 2 national ranking.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nFox currently holds a National \"B\" License with the United States Soccer Foundation and his 'Premier License' with United Soccer Coaches.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nFox, a native of Stone, Staffordshire, England, is a 2009 graduate of Messiah University (formerly Messiah College) in Mechanicsburg, Pa., where he earned a bachelor's degree in Marketing. He and his wife, Emily (a former Messiah College Field Hockey standout), have two daughters, Cassidy (5) and Addison (3).\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cstrong>WHAT THEY ARE SAYING ABOUT CHRIS FOX\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr />\r\n\"Chris Fox is a terrific young coach. His teams play with sophistication and purpose. He is meticulous in his methods, and those methods will serve the student-athletes at Bowling Green extremely well. When we learned of our NCAA Tournament first-round opponent, I immediately knew that we'd be competing against a possession-based, organized team. Credit to Chris for turning Morehead around in such a short period of time. Success will certainly continue at BGSU!\"\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cem>– Brian \u003C/em>\u003Cem>Pensky\u003C/em>\u003Cem>, Head Women's Soccer Coach, Florida State University (2023 national champions and national coaching staff of the year)\u003C/em>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"Chris is a rising star within our profession, so kudos to BG on the great hire. Chris is both innovative and meticulous in his planning and approach. His game model is forward-thinking and ambitious, and I've been thoroughly impressed with how he's implemented it at multiple programs. Chris is incredibly hard working, and he is a proven recruiter and culture-builder. I'm confident that he will build upon the strong legacy of Bowling Green soccer!\"\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cem>– Nate Lie, Head Women's Soccer Coach, University of Kansas\u003C/em>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"The job Chris did at Morehead was remarkable, winning a title in only his second season. The planning and detail that goes into his process is exceptional. His ideas around the game and the brand of soccer that he implements are truly enjoyable to watch. His teams are always bought in, compete hard and play a possession-based style that is as well executed as any team at the collegiate level. I fully expect him to not only compete for championships at BGSU, but to do so with an exciting, attractive brand of soccer.\"\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cem>– Paul \u003C/em>\u003Cem>Babba\u003C/em>\u003Cem>, Head Women's Soccer Coach, Bellarmine University\u003C/em>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"Bowling Green nailed it with this hire! Chris is one of the best positional play coaches in college soccer. The players are going to love his approach to the game. They will develop by having the ball and making decisions. His game model is backed up with data, video, and leadership development. He will take advantage of great soccer in the state of Ohio in recruiting and will scan the globe for the right talent to add to that. They will have a clear identity as a program which will lead to results!\"\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cem>– Joshua Walters, Sr, Head Women's Soccer Coach, James Madison University\u003C/em>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"Under the guidance of Chris, I've not only grown as a player but also as a person. Samuel joined the Bowling Green State University women’s soccer coaching staff in January of 2025. Samuel, who came to BGSU after two seasons on the staff at Coastal Carolina University, officially began his duties on Friday, Jan. 10.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nInitially named an assistant coach, Samuel was quickly promoted to associate head coach in August of 2025.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n“I am thrilled to add Steven to our staff,” said BGSU head coach Chris Fox at the time of Samuel's hiring. “He is a highly motivated individual with a wealth of experience at the Division I level. Steven is a tireless recruiter, has a growth mindset and firmly believes in positional play soccer. I have no doubt he will hit the ground running and be an integral part of what we are trying to build here in Bowling Green!”\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn the 2024 season, Samuel helped the Chanticleers to an overall record of 8-7-6, a five-win improvement over the previous season and the program’s highest win total since 2018. CCU posted a winning record for the first time since 2017.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThe 2024 team, picked to finish 12th in the 14-team Sun Belt Conference in the preseason coaches poll, finished 3-3-4 in league action and earned the seventh seed for the Sun Belt Tournament.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn the tourney, the Chants pulled a quarterfinal-round upset over the number-two seed to advance to the semifinals for the first time since 2017.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n“I am grateful to be a part of the Bowling Green State University family,” said Samuel. “I would like to thank Coach Fox for this opportunity. From the conversations I had with Chris, Derek (van der Merwe) and Erik (Hildebrand), it is clear that this is a special community with great people.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n“I look forward to contributing to the vision Chris has for the women’s soccer program. I am excited to meet the team and get started this spring.”\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nSamuel was one of just 30 coaches at all levels named to the 2023-24 class of the United Soccer Coaches 30 Under 30 Program, which is a year-long education and mentorship opportunity designed to support up-and-coming members of the coaching profession who are 30 years of age or younger.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nBefore joining head coach Jo Chubb’s staff at CCU in February of 2023,  Samuel spent one season at Old Dominion, serving as a volunteer assistant coach for the Monarchs. ODU captured the 2022 Sun Belt Conference crown in their first season in the league.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nIn Samuel’s lone year at ODU, he helped the program to records of 9-9-3 overall and 5-4-1 in league play. The Monarchs finished the season strong, winning each of the final two regular-season matches and then running the table in the 2022 Sun Belt Tournament with wins over the number three (Arkansas State), number two (South Alabama) and number four seed (James Madison) to capture the tourney title.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nSamuel helped coach Carla Morich and Ece Turkoglu, who both earned All-Sun Belt first-team honors and were joined by Riley Kennett in picking up United Soccer Coaches Association All-Southeast Region team accolades.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nPrior to his year at ODU, Samuel spent two seasons at Mount St Mary’s University in Maryland. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn his time with the Mountaineers, Samuel worked directly with the attacking unit and oversaw a consistent improvement in offensive production in 2020 and 2021. The 22 goals scored in the 2021 season were the most since 2012. Samuel helped develop five All-Northeast Conference Team honorees in the 2020 season, the highest single-season total in program history. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nSamuel also spent two seasons as an undergraduate assistant coach at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC). Among his responsibilities were assisting the coaching staff in opposition scouting, and in both individual and team training sessions, as well as helping with video analysis and ID Camps.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn addition to his time at the Mount and UMBC, Samuel has served as a head coach for numerous youth teams, most notably at Ellicott City SC, FC Frederick, and Virginia Rush.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nHe holds a United States Soccer Federation (USSF) “C” Coaching license and a United Soccer Coaches Level 3 Goalkeeping Diploma. \u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nA native of Lagos, Nigeria, Samuel graduated from UMBC in 2019 with a degree in psychology.
